items.followUp: What information is usually written inside the head section of an HTML document?

rubric.why: Identifies the section being defined.
rubric.description: States that it is the head part of an HTML document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the head section.

rubric.why: Explains what the section contains or how it appears.
rubric.description: Mentions document information such as the title or metadata, which is generally not displayed in the page body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant content or display detail.

modelAnswer: The head section is the part of an HTML document enclosed by <head> and </head>.
It contains information about the document, such as its title, and is generally not displayed as page content.

items.followUp: Name and describe four common symbols used in a flowchart.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the flowchart terminal symbol and its use.
rubric.description: Identifies the oval/terminal symbol for start or end.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and purpose.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the process symbol.
rubric.description: Identifies the rectangle as a process or instruction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and purpose.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the input/output symbol.
rubric.description: Identifies the parallelogram for input or output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and purpose.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the decision symbol.
rubric.description: Identifies the diamond for a decision or condition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and purpose.

modelAnswer: 1. Oval (terminal): represents the start or end of a flowchart.
2. Rectangle (process): represents an instruction or processing step.
3. Parallelogram (input/output): represents data entering or leaving the system.
4. Diamond (decision): represents a condition with alternative paths, such as Yes/No.

items.followUp: Define a computer network and explain the difference between a point-to-point and a multipoint connection.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of a network.
rubric.description: Defines a network as connected computers or devices that communicate or share resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing connected devices that communicate or share resources.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of a point-to-point connection.
rubric.description: States that a point-to-point connection links two devices through a dedicated link.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the two-device dedicated-link idea.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of a multipoint connection.
rubric.description: States that a multipoint connection allows more than two devices to share a link.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shared-link idea.

rubric.why: Checks the distinction between the two connection types.
rubric.description: Distinguishes a link between two devices from a link shared by several devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct comparison.

modelAnswer: A computer network is a group of interconnected computers and other devices that communicate and share data or resources.
In a point-to-point connection, a dedicated communication link connects two devices.
In a multipoint connection, more than two devices share a single communication link.
Thus, a point-to-point link is dedicated to two devices, while a multipoint link is shared.

items.followUp: What is encryption, and how does it help protect online communication?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of encryption.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption converts readable information into coded form using a method or key.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the conversion of readable data into coded data.

rubric.why: Checks the privacy benefit of encryption.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption prevents unauthorized people from reading data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the confidentiality benefit.

rubric.why: Checks a practical everyday use or example.
rubric.description: Identifies sensitive information, such as passwords or financial details, that encryption helps protect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example of protected information.

rubric.why: Checks the importance of encryption during internet use.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption helps secure online communication or data sent over the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking encryption with safer online activity.

modelAnswer: Encryption is the process of converting readable information (plain text) into coded, unreadable information (cipher text), usually using a key.
It helps prevent unauthorized people from reading private information.
It protects sensitive details such as passwords, personal information and financial data.
Encryption therefore helps keep online communication and data transmissions secure.

items.followUp: Why is a large problem often divided into smaller subproblems when designing an algorithm?

rubric.why: Checks the division part of the divide-and-conquer strategy.
rubric.description: States that a complex problem is split into smaller, manageable parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the problem is divided into smaller parts.

rubric.why: Checks the benefit and solving process.
rubric.description: Explains that smaller parts are easier to solve, and their solutions can be combined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant benefit or the combining of subproblem solutions.

modelAnswer: We use the divide-and-conquer strategy to split a complex problem into smaller, manageable subproblems.
The subproblems are easier to solve separately, and their solutions can be combined to solve the original problem.
